title: Make a Blazor search box filter as you type
summary: @bind writes back only when the field loses focus. @bind:event="oninput" makes it per keystroke, and @bind:after runs the server search.

turns.user: product search doesnt filter while typing. only after enter or clicking outside the box. want it live

assistant.body: Great observation! With only @bind on an <input>, the value is written back to query on the onchange event. For a text input, onchange fires only when the field loses focus or you press Enter. In other words, the characters you are typing have not reached the C# side yet. Add @bind:event="oninput" and query updates on every keystroke, so Filtered is recomputed on each render.

turns.user: works. but we have 50k products and they want it off the client memory. search on the server every keystroke. also i added @oninput and now it wont build

assistant.body: Sure. Putting @oninput next to @bind:event="oninput" writes the same oninput attribute twice on one element, so the build fails. To run code after the value is written back, use @bind:after, added in .NET 7. It accepts a method that returns Task, so the server search is awaited there. Note: this searches on every keystroke. With that many products, a debounce is worth adding.
